resources.string: A schematic of typical adult, nonpregnant anatomy. The moving highlight traces anatomical connections, not fluid flow. Sections and magnifications are not to scale.
From the uterine cavity outward: the endometrium lines the cavity, the myometrium forms the thick smooth muscle wall, and the thin perimetrium covers the outer surface where serosa is present.

The internal os connects the uterine cavity to the cervical canal. The external os opens into the vagina. The cervix has a glandular canal lining and a wall rich in collagen, distinct from the thick uterine muscle above.

The vagina extends from around the cervix to the vaginal opening. Its folded squamous lining can flatten as the wall stretches, above a layer of smooth muscle. The inset illustrates that change in fold depth.
This inner lining borders the uterine cavity.
Interlacing smooth muscle makes up most of the uterine body wall.
This thin serosal coat covers part of the outer uterine surface.
The upper narrowing where the uterine cavity meets the cervical canal.
The passage through the cervix has a glandular lining and lies within collagen-rich tissue.
The lower end of the cervical canal opens into the upper vagina.
